data.situation: On Wednesday, Nina and Sam stood outside the library with a small stack of leaflets. The notice in the town hall had been the first step in their campaign for a usable bench. Now Sam began to distribute the leaflets to people leaving the library. A woman carrying groceries stopped to talk; a man waiting for his daughter pointed to the narrow gap between the bench and the wall behind it. At first, Sam asked only whether people wanted the bench repaired. Almost everyone said yes, but the answers did not explain how the space was used. Nina suggested that they adopt a different way of collecting comments. They asked where people would sit and which part of the pavement they needed to pass through. One neighbour suggested moving the bench farther along the wall to a wider part of the pavement. Sam marked its present position and the suggested one with arrows on a copy of the photograph while Nina wrote down the comments. The following evening, they returned to the town hall and went upstairs to the meeting room. A name card with “Chair” below the name helped Nina identify the person chairing the meeting. She placed the photograph with arrows where the members could see it. They needed to assess how the present and suggested locations for the bench would affect the people using the pavement. Nina explained the comments they had gathered, including the man’s concern about the gap by the wall. Before the meeting ended, the members asked for a clearer photograph of that gap behind the bench. Nina put the papers back in her bag, with that request written on top. The outcome was still uncertain. At the noticeboard downstairs, she added a short message saying they would take the photograph on Saturday and share the decision when it came. Sam held the remaining leaflets while she pinned the message beneath Wednesday’s notice.
data.easySummary: The residents’ campaign continues outside the library. Nina and Sam distribute leaflets and adopt a different way of collecting comments, using more specific questions. A neighbour suggests moving the bench along the wall to a wider place. At the meeting, a name card marked “Chair” helps Nina identify the chair. The council members assess the present and suggested locations. They ask for a clearer photograph of the gap behind the bench, so the outcome is still uncertain.
data.easySummaryZh: 居民活动继续来到图书馆外。妮娜和萨姆分发传单，采用另一种收集意见的方式，提出更具体的问题。一位邻居建议沿墙把长椅移到较宽的地方。会议中，标有“Chair（主持人）”的姓名卡帮助妮娜认出主持人。议员评估原位置和建议位置。他们还要一张更清晰的照片，看清长椅后方的空隙，因此结果仍未确定。

retrievalPrompts.cue: A neighbour asks what you have been doing since the notice went up. Explain how the leaflets fit into the activity and who receives them.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 一位邻居问告示贴出后你们做了什么。说明传单是活动的哪一步，以及发给谁。
acceptableAnswers: Our campaign includes the notice and conversations outside the library. We distribute the leaflets to people leaving the library to invite their comments.

retrievalPrompts.cue: The first question produced many yes answers but little detail. A neighbour suggested a wider place farther along the wall. Tell Sam how to collect useful comments and which two locations the council members need to judge.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 第一个问题得到很多“是”的回答，但几乎没有细节。一位邻居建议沿墙移到更远的较宽处。告诉萨姆怎样收集有用意见，以及议员需要判断哪两个位置。
acceptableAnswers: We should adopt a different way of collecting comments and ask how people use the pavement. The members need to assess how the present and suggested bench locations would affect them.

retrievalPrompts.function: The name card and the papers
retrievalPrompts.cue: You reach the meeting room and see a name card marked “Chair”. Afterwards, a neighbour asks whether the bench will be repaired or moved. Explain how you find the person and what you can currently say about the decision.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 你到会议室，看到一张标有“Chair（主持人）”的姓名卡。会后邻居问长椅会不会修好或移动。说明你如何认出主持人，以及现在能怎样说明决定的情况。
acceptableAnswers: The name card marked “Chair” helps me identify the person chairing the meeting. The outcome is still uncertain; the council has asked for a clearer photograph of the gap behind the bench.

transferPrompt.cue: An office asks whether staff want a new shared kitchen. Most people say yes, but no one has discussed cleaning or space. The manager has not decided. Explain how to collect useful comments and what to tell colleagues about the result.
transferPrompt.cueZh: 办公室问员工是否想要新共用厨房，大多数人说想，但还没讨论清洁或空间。经理尚未决定。说明怎样收集有用意见，以及如何向同事说明结果。
acceptableAnswers: We should adopt a different way of collecting comments and ask about cleaning and space. The manager needs to assess the effects, and the outcome is still uncertain.
